LESSON: STORYTELLING AND ANIMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.7: Storytelling and Animation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Storytelling and Animation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can storytelling be made interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe techniques used in storytelling
2. explain qualities of a good flipbook
3. compose a 3 to 5- minute story addressing an issue in society
4. create a flipbook animation for storytelling
5. perform a 3 to 5- minute story before an audience

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: STORYTELLING AND ANIMATION
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Storytelling and Animation helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: STORYTELLING AND ANIMATION
Study Storytelling and Animation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe techniques used in storytelling

What this means
In this part you learn to describe techniques used in storytelling. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe techniques used in storytelling.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Storytelling and Animation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe techniques used in storytelling. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain qualities of a good flipbook

What this means
In this part you learn to explain qualities of a good flipbook. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain qualities of a good flipbook.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Storytelling and Animation in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain qualities of a good flipbook. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Compose a 3 to 5- minute story addressing an issue in society

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a 3 to 5- minute story addressing an issue in society. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a 3 to 5- minute story addressing an issue in society.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a 3 to 5- minute story addressing an issue in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Create a flipbook animation for storytelling

What this means
In this part you learn to create a flipbook animation for storytelling. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a flipbook animation for storytelling.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Storytelling and Animation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a flipbook animation for storytelling. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Perform a 3 to 5- minute story before an audience

What this means
In this part you learn to perform a 3 to 5- minute story before an audience. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform a 3 to 5- minute story before an audience.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Storytelling and Animation in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform a 3 to 5- minute story before an audience. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Storytelling and Animation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Storytelling and Animation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe techniques used in storytelling)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Storytelling and Animation in your own words. (skill: explain qualities of a good flipbook)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: compose a 3 to 5- minute story addressing an issue in society)

Example 4: Show how “Storytelling and Animation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: create a flipbook animation for storytelling)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Storytelling and Animation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe techniques used in storytelling.
3. Practise this skill: explain qualities of a good flipbook.
4. Practise this skill: compose a 3 to 5- minute story addressing an issue in society.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Storytelling and Animation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Storytelling and Animation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Storytelling and Animation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can storytelling be made interesting?
2. How can flip book animation be used in storytelling?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Storytelling and Animation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe techniques used in storytelling.
5. Be able to: explain qualities of a good flipbook.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
